artifacts.summary: Evaluates whether validate-no-task-references.sh should resolve task-ref-ok markers against the full on-disk file; recommends region-aware (not whole-file-boolean) resolution via a depth-counter marker parse, a reconstructed post-edit merge for Edit calls only, no on-disk read for Write calls, graceful degradation for new/unreadable files, and a six-case test matrix.

memory_candidates.content: In agent-system/extensions/core, hooks/validate-no-task-references.sh (write-time PreToolUse gate) and scripts/check-task-references.sh (repo-wide lint) share scripts/lib/task-reference-patterns.sh for task-reference citation detection and task-ref-ok marker exemption. The lint already reads whole files via git ls-files + strip_exempt_regions, but the hook's Edit path only ever sees tool_input.new_string (a snippet), never the on-disk file -- so a file-wide marker pair living outside the edited span is invisible to the hook even though the lint already honors it. The Write path has no such gap: tool_input.content for a Write already IS the complete new file, so strip_exempt_regions already resolves markers whole-file there today. Any future fix for the Edit-path gap must reconstruct the post-edit file (on-disk content with old_string substituted by new_string) and must never let the Write path fall back to reading on-disk content, since on-disk is the stale pre-write state for a Write call.

task-reference-patterns.sh's strip_exempt_regions uses a boolean in_block flag (not a depth counter) to track task-ref-ok:begin/:end spans. This has two latent defects worth remembering when touching marker-stripping code generally: (1) an unterminated begin with no matching end exempts everything from that point to EOF of whatever content it is handed, rather than failing closed; (2) nested or overlapping begin/end pairs are not counted correctly by a boolean flag -- a depth counter (increment on begin, decrement on end, never below 0, and a validity check that depth returns to 0 by EOF) is the correct fix and should be the default approach whenever implementing begin/end marker-span stripping in this codebase, rather than a simple toggle.
